          <script>
            // Synchronize playback of every .video-grid clip on the active slide.
            // Pauses everything else so background slides don't compete for decode.
            function gridVideosOn(slide) {
              return slide ? Array.from(slide.querySelectorAll('.video-grid video')) : [];
            }
            function syncGridVideos(slide) {
              if (!slide) return;
              document.querySelectorAll('.video-grid video').forEach(v => v.pause());
              const vids = gridVideosOn(slide);
              vids.forEach(v => { v.currentTime = 0; });
              // Slight delay so seeks resolve before play() to keep them aligned.
              setTimeout(() => vids.forEach(v => v.play().catch(() => {})), 50);
            }
            // Click any grid video to toggle pause/play across the whole grid,
            // re-syncing to t=0 on resume so the comparison stays aligned.
            function toggleGrid(slide) {
              const vids = gridVideosOn(slide);
              if (!vids.length) return;
              const anyPlaying = vids.some(v => !v.paused);
              if (anyPlaying) {
                vids.forEach(v => v.pause());
              } else {
                vids.forEach(v => { v.currentTime = 0; });
                setTimeout(() => vids.forEach(v => v.play().catch(() => {})), 50);
              }
            }
            function bindGridClick(slide) {
              gridVideosOn(slide).forEach(v => {
                if (v.dataset.gridClickBound) return;
                v.style.cursor = 'pointer';
                v.addEventListener('click', e => {
                  e.preventDefault();
                  e.stopPropagation();
                  toggleGrid(slide);
                });
                v.dataset.gridClickBound = '1';
              });
            }
            if (window.Reveal) {
              Reveal.on('ready', e => { bindGridClick(e.currentSlide); syncGridVideos(e.currentSlide); });
              Reveal.on('slidechanged', e => { bindGridClick(e.currentSlide); syncGridVideos(e.currentSlide); });
            }
          </script>

## Two codec regimes

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Legacy: h264 / gbrp / 720×540 / 500 fps**

- 6,936 files (62% of raw)
- 17.32 B frames (90% of all frames)
- 9,622 hours
- Lossy h264_nvenc, full-range GBR
- **This is the transcode target.**
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Legacy: mpeg4 / yuv420p / various**

- 4,266 files (38%)
- 1.82 B frames (10%)
- ~5,200 hours
- 720×540@120 fps NM (older), 800×600@30-60 fps foraging-specialty, 1440×1080@20 fps CellTypeLUT pupil, …
- Need to look into these videos more.
:::
:::

## Picking an instance family

::: {.small-table}
| family            | per-vCPU @ full load | 96-vCPU agg. | spot ~$/hr  | est. **$/batch**  |
|-------------------|---------------------:|-------------:|------------:|------------------:|
| **c8a** (Zen 5)   | **65 fps**           | **~6,200**   | **$1.55**   | **~$1,290** ⭐    |
| c7a (Zen 4)       | 46 fps               | ~4,440       | $1.40       | ~$1,630           |
| c8g (Graviton 4)  | 34 fps               | ~3,280       | $1.10       | ~$1,730           |
| c8i (Granite Rap.)| 37 fps               | ~3,500       | $1.65       | ~$2,430           |
:::

::: {.smaller}
4-family bake-off on c-class .2xlarge, slow/CRF 18, same input file (`side_camera_left.avi`). Each instance fully loaded (n=8 of 8 vCPUs). Spot prices are recent us-west-2 estimates. **c8a wins on throughput AND $/throughput.** Zen 5's wider front-end + AMD's libx264-friendly SMT beat Intel's Granite Rapids (modest gen-over-gen) and Graviton 4's no-SMT model (per-core memory-bandwidth limited).
:::

## Cost & wallclock

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
**c8a.24xlarge spot, slow / CRF 18, 18.6 B frames**

::: {.small-table}
| fleet           | wallclock | spot cost | notes |
|-----------------|----------:|----------:|-------|
| 1× c8a.24xl     | ~35 days  | ~$1,290   | one instance, long tail |
| 4× c8a.24xl     | ~9 days   | ~$1,290   | recommended ops sweet spot |
| 8× c8a.24xl     | ~4.5 days | ~$1,290   | tight wallclock, more orchestration |
:::

Spot cost is essentially constant in compute-hours — fanout trades wallclock for instance count at flat $/batch.

Add ~4% for chunked-encoding overhead (preemption resilience) → **final batch ≈ $1,350**.
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
**Output footprint**

- Input: ~217 TB (h264_gbrp .avi)
- Output: **~75 TB** (OFFLINE_8BIT .mp4, ~3× compression)
- Storage delta: **−142 TB** archival savings

**Preemption resilience**

- ~20-min encode chunks (closed GOP)
- Atomic manifest (DynamoDB), per-chunk lease
- Concat with `-c copy` at the end (no re-encode)
- Lost work per spot kill: bounded to one chunk
:::
:::

- [ ] **Sign-off** on the transcoding budget (~$3.5 k EC2 spot + storage delta)
- [ ] **Decision** on the 8 `45_AP_*_ML_*` files: confirm they're imaging (not behavior) and move out of `behavior_videos/`
- [ ] **Catalog** the 68 bare-numeric `video.avi` assets into docdb so they get the AIND prefix + transcode treatment
- [ ] **Schedule**: pipeline launch window (manifest + atomic writes + sharding already designed in the cascade-benchmark scratch dir)

## Method

1. **Scan**: walk the weekly **S3 Inventory** for `aind-open-data` (~3.7 k gzipped CSV shards / 377 GB) and grep for `.avi` keys.
2. **Filter & categorize**: derive platform / camera-type / project from the key and join against docdb.
3. **Probe**: ffprobe every raw AVI via HTTPS range requests (≈ 1-2 MB per file) → codec, pix_fmt, resolution, fps, frame count, color tags.
